title: IRIS: A 8.55 mJ/frame Spatial Computing SoC for Real-time Interactable-Rendering and Surface-aware-Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: Real-time spatial computing with 3D Gaussian Splatting requires specialized hardware for low-latency, energy-efficient rendering and surface modeling.
motivation: XR/spatial computing demands real-time rendering at 8-12 fps while maintaining low power envelope for mobile devices, driving need for specialized SoCs.
method: IRIS is a specialized chip designed specifically for 3D Gaussian Splatting, a technique that represents 3D scenes as millions of overlapping soft blob shapes. It has dedicated hardware components for three tasks: converting blobs to screen pixels (Gaussian rasterization), mathematically optimizing the rendering quality (differentiable rendering), and detecting solid surfaces in the scene (surface reconstruction). By building the entire chip around these specific tasks, it achieves real-time performance at only 8.55 millijoules per frame.
key_novelty: IRIS is the first chip designed specifically for 3D Gaussian Splatting, with hardware and software built together to optimize rendering and surface modeling.
contributions: Specialized SoC architecture for Gaussian Splatting rendering
Real-time interactable rendering with surface awareness
